one_line_purpose: A high-performance, in-memory key-value cache server built with Python and asyncio, communicating over raw TCP sockets.
problem_solved: Provides a fast, in-memory key-value storage solution that supports caching features like Time-To-Live (TTL) and Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction, handling concurrent client connections over a custom TCP protocol.
architecture_summary: The KV-Cache server is structured into three main layers: Network, Protocol, and Cache. The Network Layer (tcp_server.py) uses asyncio to provide an asynchronous TCP server, handling multiple concurrent client connections. The Protocol Layer (parser.py, commands.py) defines and parses custom text-based commands (PUT, GET, DELETE, EXISTS, QUIT) and formats responses. The Cache Layer (store.py, eviction.py) manages the in-memory key-value data with support for Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration and Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policies. Clients interact with the server over raw TCP sockets.
key_features: High-performance asynchronous TCP server using asyncio
Custom text-based network protocol (PUT, GET, DELETE, EXISTS, QUIT)
Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy for cache management
Configurable host, port, and maximum cache size
notable_code_decisions: Utilizes asyncio for non-blocking I/O and concurrent client handling in the TCP server.
Employs collections.OrderedDict for the KVStore and LRUEvictionPolicy to achieve O(1) average-case time complexity for cache operations and efficient LRU ordering.
Divides functionality into distinct Network, Protocol, and Cache layers for modularity.
Configuration parameters are managed through src/config/settings.py and can be overridden by environment variables or command-line arguments.
Expired keys are handled with lazy cleanup during GET, DELETE, and EXISTS operations, with an additional cleanup_expired method for proactive removal.
Dockerfile is configured to run the server as a non-root user (appuser) for improved security.
tradeoffs_and_limitations: In-memory storage means data is not persistent across server restarts.
Designed for a single server instance, lacking inherent distributed caching, replication, or sharding mechanisms.
The custom raw TCP protocol requires client-side implementation specific to this server, not compatible with standard protocols like HTTP or Redis protocol.
Only supports basic string key-value pairs; no complex data structures like lists, sets, or hashes.
LRU eviction, while efficient, may not be optimal for all workload patterns.
what_it_demonstrates: Building a high-performance asynchronous network server using Python's asyncio. Implementing core caching concepts such as in-memory key-value storage, Time-To-Live (TTL), and Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction. Designing and parsing a custom network protocol over raw TCP sockets. Containerizing applications with Docker. Performing basic load testing and benchmarking. Setting up an application for cloud deployment (e.g., AWS EC2). Practicing structured project organization, testing, and dependency management.
